text: cat /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/uv/msg15.txt: ailed open warns in the words of the `fopen` this is built from and at the prelude's own line — `gzopen("nope.gz", "r")` on line 1 says `Warning: fopen(nope.gz): ... on line 4` where php says `gzopen(nope.gz): ... on line 1`. The VALUE, `false`, matches; warning with a wrong name was preferred to suppressing the inner warning and going silent. And one level down, elephc's own `fopen("compress.zlib://nope.gz")` names the underlying path where php names the URL — not this prelude's, and fixing it there fixes it here. `gzencode` and `gzdecode` are deliberately NOT included. They are string functions with gzip framing rather than stream functions, and their header carries an OS byte that comes from the platform's zlib — 0x13 here, and not verifiable for the Linux targets from this host. The framing is fully measured and recorded for that follow-up; the rest of the family does not wait on it.
